title: Department of Homeland Security: Evaluation of DHS' Information Security Program for Fiscal Year 2024
publisher: Department of Homeland Security Office of Inspector General
summary: DHS OIG rated the department information-security program effective for FY 2024. Entity use: DHS's FY 2024 FISMA evaluation extends the panel with an effective result. GAO's 2025 review separately identifies CDM guidance, data-quality, endpoint, and cloud-asset gaps; the two records describe coexisting control conditions, not cause and effect.
key_findings: Identify and Respond were rated Level 5; Protect, Detect, and Recover were rated Level 4, with selected-component and selected-system testing boundaries.
Temporal role: DHS and CISA continued operating the government-wide CDM program for asset visibility and network monitoring.
Attribution: DHS OIG reports the department result; GAO independently reports CDM implementation constraints.
why_it_matters: This entity-matched record adds a named driver, control, input, constraint, or later observation to a Phase 56B panel without treating sequence as causal proof.
ftfn_relevance: Preserves the parent panel's stable entity identifier.
Separates baseline, intervention or constraint, and observed outcome.
Records independent validation, alternative explanations, and the causal-inference boundary.
evidence_limits: The department-wide result does not represent identical control maturity or operating risk across every DHS component and system.
Two independent oversight bodies support the coexistence of the records, not a causal relationship.
No ranking, composite score, readiness score, or causal estimate is supported.
